_label: ODYSSEY II transfer test of R-sparse-active-expert-gather across the WHOLE measured MoE population (12 bodies). The rule's precondition holds everywhere; its CONCLUSION does not.
_evidence: MEASURED from safetensors headers -- expert mass separated from non-expert mass by tensor name, no GPU, no load.
rule_under_test: R-sparse-active-expert-gather -- 'kind == moe AND experts_per_tok << experts -> candidate native expert-gather (move only active experts, not the full inventory)'

RESULT.transferred: 10 of 12 bodies sit at 4.6-13.5% active, where gather is decisive.
RESULT.FAILED_ON: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (and its abliterated twin) at 32.8% active -- despite having the SPARSEST top-k ratio in the whole population (10 of 512 experts, 1.95%). The rule's precondition is satisfied more strongly there than anywhere else, and the conclusion is still wrong.
RESULT.why: the rule silently assumes the expert organ IS most of the model. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next carries 56.69B of NON-EXPERT parameters (31.5% of the body) against GLM-4.5-Air's 7.8% and Kimi-K3's 3.8%. Gather cannot touch shared mass, so no routing sparsity can push active below it.

REFINED_LAW.validated: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: 31.5% + 68.5% * (10/512) = 31.5% + 1.34% = 32.84%, against 32.8% measured independently from tensor arithmetic. The identity reproduces the measurement.
REFINED_LAW.consequence: the gather lever's ceiling is 1 - non_expert_fraction, and the top-k ratio only controls how much of the REMAINDER it captures. A body with heavy shared mass is gather-resistant no matter how sparse its routing looks, so the rule's real condition is on EXPERT MASS FRACTION, not on k << E.
REFINED_LAW.practical_rule: before spending a gather implementation, measure expert_mass/total. Above ~90% (Kimi-K3, GLM-4.5-Air) gather is nearly the whole battle; near ~68% (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) a third of the body stays resident whatever routing does, and the shared organ becomes the primary Gravity target instead.
